hints: Remember what alkaline aqueous iodine is testing for, think iodoform test and the yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$.
An alcohol only gives a positive result if it contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group, a methyl group directly attached to the carbon bearing the -OH.
Sketch or visualise each carbon skeleton and check which one has $\text{CH}_3$ next to $\text{CH(OH)}$, that one will be oxidised in situ to a methyl ketone and then give the precipitate.
walkthrough:
**Recall the iodoform test**

Great spot, yellow precipitate with alkaline aqueous iodine means a positive tri-iodomethane (iodoform) test.

Test result:
$$\text{positive} \rightarrow \text{yellow precipitate of } \text{CHI}_3$$

**Know the structural requirement for alcohols**

For an alcohol, the test is positive only if it has the group $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$.

In the reaction the secondary alcohol is first oxidised to a methyl ketone, which then reacts:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}- \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{CH}_3\text{CO}- \xrightarrow{\text{I}_2 / \text{NaOH}} \text{CHI}_3$$

**Check each C5 isomer**

Now look for $\text{CH}_3$ attached directly to the $\text{C-OH}$ carbon.

$\text{3-methylbutan-2-ol}$ is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_3$, which clearly contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, so it gives the yellow precipitate.

options.A: Incorrect. 2,2-dimethylpropan-1-ol is $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCH}_2\text{OH}$, a primary alcohol with no $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group. It cannot be oxidised to a methyl ketone, so no $\text{CHI}_3$ forms.
options.B: Incorrect. 2-methylbutan-2-ol is $\text{CH}_3\text{C(OH)(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, a tertiary alcohol. It has no H on the C-OH carbon so it is not oxidised and does not contain $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, so the test is negative.
options.C: Correct. 3-methylbutan-2-ol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_3$. It contains the key $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ unit, so it is oxidised to $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_3$ and then gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate with $\text{I}_2$ in $\text{NaOH}$.
options.D: Incorrect. Pentan-3-ol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Although it is a secondary alcohol, the group next to C-OH is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-$, not $\text{CH}_3-$. It is oxidised to pentan-3-one, which is not a methyl ketone, so no precipitate forms. This is a common trap.
